newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond issuers rush to beat the clock.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond issuers rush to beat the clock.

text.p: Corporate bond issuers are rushing to beat the clock, bringing new debt issues at a rapid rate as 1996 ticks away, dealers said.
"We should see some more supply this week and then I think it'll be wrapped up for the year," one high-grade syndicate source said on Wednesday.
High-grade syndicate sources said they had heard that Walt Disney & Co was getting set to issue a $500 million 10-year debt offering via JP Morgan Securities.
Among other deals expected are a number of bank preferred securities, dealers said.
Among Tuesday's debt offerings, Rite Aid Corp's three-part debt offering which was very well received by the market tightened when freed to trade, dealers said.
The multi-tranche debt offering was boosted in size to $1.0 billion, from an initial $600 million to meet strong demand, they added.

"Rite Aid's new deal is doing very well," said one high-grade syndicate source. "The 10-year notes tightened a couple of basis points since pricing and were quoted at 71 (bid), 69 (offer)...look for all of the issues to tighten."
Among other investment grade offerings, Scholastic Corp is expected to issue $125 million in seven-year notes via Goldman Sachs.
Also, American Re Corp is expected to tap the market with $500 million in 30-year noncallable 144A debt also via Goldman Sachs & Co. The deal is expected to be rated Aa1/AA.

Meanwhile, dealers said with not much left to the calendar year and the Christmas and New Year's holidays approaching the bulk of supply is likely to come this week while desks are still fully staffed.
Rite Aid issued $350 million of 6.70 percent five-year debt, $300 million of 7.125 percent 10-year bonds and $300 million in 7.70 percent 30-year bonds via Goldman Sachs.
Also, Citicorp's capital securities due 2027, which priced to yield 120 basis points over Treasuries did very well when free to trade, syndicate sources said.
Among upcoming high-yield debt offerings the following are expected, dealers said.
Wilshire Financial Services Group Inc's $75 million in seven-year notes.
Maxxam Group Holdings' $100 million in 144A notes due 2003 via Bear Stearns & Co. Price talk on the issue is 10.75 to 12.0 percent.
Mechala Group Jamaica Ltd's $75 million in three-year 144A notes.
Willcox & Gibbs' $85 million in seven-year 144A notes via Dillon Read & Co.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 7/32 at 98-3/32 to yield 6.65 percent compared with Tuesday's 6.66 percent at the close.
